messages:
maya: Heads-up — after HF->Redwood import of knight-7b we started seeing stray <|pad|> tokens peppered into generated text. Repro quick: decode of a short prompt returns `\n<|pad|> Hello` instead of `Hello`.

maya: Steps I ran: `redwood-import --src hf://username/knight-7b --output /models/knight-7b/redwood` then `redwood-deploy --model /models/knight-7b/redwood`. No errors during import.

maya: Inspecting tokenizer files showed weird ordering in added_tokens.json vs tokenizer.json. snippet: ```
added_tokens.json => [{"id":50260,"content":"<|pad|>"}, {"id":50261,"content":"<|special1|>"}]
tokenizer.json shows vocab_size:50257 and special token ids: {"bos":0,"eos":50256}
```

liam: :face_with_monocle: sounds like an id-offset: added_tokens inserted at the end but our loader expects added tokens to be appended without reassigning existing ids. If tokenizer.vocab was rebuilt, ids might have wrapped or shifted.

liam: Can you run `python -c "from token_utils import inspect; print(inspect('path/to/tokenizer'))"` and paste the first/last 8 ids?

maya: Pasted output: ```
0: "<|bos|>"
1: " the"
...
50256: "<|eos|>"
50257: "ä"
50260: "<|pad|>"
```

sophie: That 50257/50260 hole is suspicious. HF conversion sometimes reassigns ids when added_tokens contains indices that collide with reserved hf offsets. Did we use `--preserve-added-token-ids`? Redwood importer currently ignores explicit ids in added_tokens.json and remaps.

jamie: We saw a similar case where quantize step changed the on-disk idx order. The quant tool rewrites the embedding table and we lost a one-off because pad got inserted before eos. Quick check: run `python -c "from redwood.tools import token_map; print(token_map.diff('hf','redwood'))"`

token-importer-bot: Import job 4591: completed. warnings: ['added_tokens.json contains explicit ids; these will be remapped', 'tokenizer.vocab size mismatch, rebuilding vocab']

maya: Ah — importer warnings were easy to miss in CI logs. That explains remap. But why decode shows pad before text? Should be ignored during generation.

liam: Likely because pad token was assigned an id that falls inside the model's decode whitelist or the generation loop doesn't treat the new pad id as special (we match by id vs by string). Two fixes: 1) ensure config.json special token ids (bos/eos/pad/unk) are updated to the remapped ids at import time; 2) adjust generation logic to check special tokens by token string when present.

sophie: For immediate hotfix, run: `redwood-token-merge --model knight-7b --preserve-specials` which will remap added_tokens but force-match known specials to their expected ids. I ran it locally and it removed leading <|pad|> tokens for chat prompts. :thumbsup:

jamie: We should add a test in onboarding pipeline: after import, run `decode("Hello")` and assert it doesn't start with any special token except bos/eos if model uses them. Also add a check that `config.json` special token ids point to tokens whose string values equal the expected tokens.

maya: Agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to importer to log remap table and to fail CI on ambiguous special-token remaps.

maya: PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8340 — includes unit test and importer warning made fatal for BOs.

liam: thanks. once PR lands, let's re-import knight-7b and run a small eval benchmark (LLamaBench subset) to ensure no perf/quality drift introduced by remap.

maya: Will do. cc @jamie for quant interplay — maybe run quantize path with a no-reorder flag if possible.

jamie: Yup will test quant flags. I suspect our 4-bit quantizer rewrites embedding ordering unless `--preserve-order` is used. I'll validate.

maya: OK, setting this to P1 for onboarding checklist until importer logs are updated.
